svg.text: WLD 205 DAY 8 — INSTRUCTOR KEY / DELIVERY GUIDE
Prerequisite metallurgy readiness. Do not begin formal ferrite/austenite/pearlite/TTT instruction here.
0–8 min — Weld / HAZ / Base-Metal Retrieval · Live Q1–3
A = weld metal. B = heat-affected zone. C = unaffected base metal.
Correction cue: the HAZ is base metal that experienced the welding thermal cycle but did not melt.
Point out the fusion boundary. Do not describe the HAZ as a layer under the plate or as deposited weld metal.
Move on when students can identify all three regions without prompting.
8–20 min — Thermal Cycle + HAZ Model
Model one clean idea: welding heat can change nearby unmelted base metal.
Use: weld metal melted/fused; HAZ did not melt; unaffected base metal lies beyond the HAZ.
Exact hardness, microstructure, or response depends on material/source, geometry/thickness, thermal cycle, restraint,
approved WPS/procedure, testing, and governing requirements as applicable.
20–38 min — HAZ Observation Cards · Live Q4–6
Card 1: visible HAZ does NOT provide exact hardness. Testing/source knowledge is required.
Card 2: angular movement under restraint raises distortion/restraint/thermal-cycle concerns. Do not name one exact cause.
Card 3: section thickness/geometry can change thermal behavior even for the same documented alloy.
Required response frame: OBSERVE → CHECK SOURCE → STATE ONLY WHAT THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTS.
Samples/photos are observation aids only. They do not establish exact grade, alloy, hardness, or microstructure.
38–52 min — Heat-Effect Cause / Consequence Map · Live Q7–9
Higher restraint → possible residual-stress, distortion, and cracking concerns.
Higher thermal conductivity → heat can be carried away faster; material-specific procedure implications must be checked.
Uncontrolled heat input/sequence → possible distortion and HAZ/property concerns.
Do not invent preheat, interpass, heat-input, sequencing, distortion-control, or acceptance values.
Those values come from the authorized controlling source when applicable.
52–60 min — Independent HAZ Exit · Live Q10–12
Q10: HAZ did not melt. Q11: exact response is source/procedure/material/joint/thickness/thermal-cycle/restraint dependent.
Q12: formal ferrite/austenite/pearlite/TTT detail belongs in the shared Level II metallurgy block after Day 22.
Remediate only the unresolved domain: Region ID | Observation vs Conclusion | Heat-Effect Reasoning | Source Control.
Standing Day 8 rule: IDENTIFY → OBSERVE → CHECK SOURCE → STATE ONLY WHAT THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTS.
